title: Nimbus Biotech - MSA/DPA & SLA review
next_steps: Redwood to send redlined MSA by 2025-12-11
Share SOC 2 type II evidence and pen test report
Provide final pricing sheet and committed capacity options
Schedule legal follow-up for 2025-12-15 at 10am PT
action_items: Maya Patel: Send redlined MSA and DPA (due: 2025-12-11)
Jordan Kim: Prepare dedicated capacity sizing and expected latency SLA numbers (due: 2025-12-12)
Liam Reyes: Share onboarding checklist and support SLAs (due: 2025-12-10)
Emily Zhang (Nimbus): Review redlines and send counter by 2025-12-13
summary: Procurement/legal review focused on MSA/DPA terms, SLAs for latency and uptime, pricing approval path, and onboarding. Redwood AE + SE walked legal and procurement through key clauses, fallback policies, and security docs; agreed to send redlines and SOC2 artifacts. Next call planned for legal reconciliation.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we really appreciate the time. I see Sara, Emily, Kevin, Aaron, and then Jordan and Liam from our side. Quick check, audio okay?
[00:08] Sara Lopez: Yep, good here.
[00:11] Emily Zhang: Yes, can hear you.
[00:13] Jordan Kim: Great. I'm Jordan, I'm the solutions engineer on the account, I'll jump in on the tech details when we get there.
[00:21] Maya Patel: Cool. Agenda: walk through the MSA/DPA outstanding points, talk SLA numbers and the dedicated vs hosted options, and pricing approvals timeline. We'll capture next steps.
[00:32] Dr. Kevin Morrell: Sounds good. Our legal flagged a few things in the DPA around data residency and retention, and our SecOps has questions on key management and logs.
[00:41] Aaron Patel: Yeah, on KMS we need to know if we can bring our own keys, and how audit logs are retained and exported.
[00:48] Maya Patel: Absolutely. On BYOK, Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations in our Private and Dedicated offerings; for Hosted we use envelope encryption - we can document the flows. I'll attach the KMS integration guide.
[01:02] Emily Zhang: Is that documented in the DPA today or is that more of an operations appendix? We need it to be contractually bound; ops notes are fine but legal prefers a clause.
[01:12] Maya Patel: Understood, we can add a contract clause referencing the KMS option for Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted we'll add wording about encryption at rest and in transit and SOC 2 controls.
[01:22] Emily Zhang: Okay. On data residency, our requirement is EU data residency for certain PHI-ish datasets - what are the options?
[01:30] Jordan Kim: For EU residency we have dedicated regions in eu-west-1 and europe-central; Redwood Private can be deployed in a VPC in your region or on-prem. For Hosted, we can route and pin workloads to those regions, but for full custody you probably want Private.
[01:46] Sara Lopez: From procurement's perspective, we need the SLA commitments; uptime and latency for our clinical tools are critical. What uptime SLA do you offer for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[01:55] Liam Reyes: Hi, Liam from CSM - our standard Hosted SLA is 99.9% for availability for production endpoints on paid tiers; Dedicated has SLA options up to 99.95% with reserved capacity and priority routing. We can include a table in the MSA.
[02:09] Dr. Kevin Morrell: And latency targets - we saw your public benchmarks but we need guaranteed p95 numbers for 2k token chat requests.
[02:17] Jordan Kim: Right, p95 depends on model and capacity. For our curated medium-sized models on Dedicated with 4 GPUs reserved, we typically hit p95 ~450-600ms at 2k tokens with batching off; with batching tuned we can get better cost but slightly higher p95. I'll put concrete numbers in the follow-up.
[02:36] Dr. Kevin Morrell: That sounds like there's a tradeoff - we need <700ms p95 for interactive clinician workflows.
[02:42] Jordan Kim: That's achievable on Dedicated with the model profile we propose; we'll include the measurement methodology and test harness so it's auditable.
[02:50] Emily Zhang: Back to DPA, limitations on use - can Redwood process PHI? We need a clause that restricts use and defines security obligations.
[02:58] Maya Patel: We can. We have customers in regulated industries; the DPA will include processing purposes, subprocessor list, and commitments on security measures. We'll share our standard DPA and can accommodate reasonable redlines.
[03:10] Aaron Patel: About subprocessors - will Redwood list cloud providers and any vector for third-party model inference? We want transparency on any external model compute.
[03:19] Jordan Kim: By default, our Hosted runs on Redwood-managed infrastructure in the cloud provider region; we list primary cloud providers in the DPA and will include a subprocessors schedule. For Dedicated/Private, customer controls the infra for Private or we can specify managed host partners.
[03:33] Sara Lopez: Price approval - procurement needs an internal PO path. What are the committed capacity options and overage pricing? We need final numbers for our finance approval.
[03:42] Maya Patel: We offer monthly reserved GPU capacity tiers with committed discounts; overage is billed at usage rates higher than the committed unit rate. I'll share the pricing sheet with tiered examples - e.g., 4-GPU reserved pool for X per month with Y% discount. We can also structure an annual commitment for better pricing.
[03:58] Emily Zhang: Can we get pricing locked for the term of the MSA?
[04:01] Maya Patel: Yes, we can include a pricing schedule with term commitments and an escalation clause. We'll reflect that in the contract appendix.
[04:09] Dr. Kevin Morrell: On termination and data return - we need a clause that guarantees export of all customer data within 30 days and secure deletion on termination with attestation.
[04:19] Maya Patel: Standard practice - we'll add export and deletion timelines in the MSA and DPA with a certificate of destruction if requested.
[04:27] Emily Zhang: Audit rights - Nimbus wants right to audit subprocessors or at least get SOC 2 reports and pen test summaries.
[04:36] Liam Reyes: We can provide SOC 2 Type II report and an executive summary of penetration testing; for on-site audits we usually allow a partnered process or redacted findings under NDA.
[04:46] Aaron Patel: On incident response and notifications - timeline for notifying customers on breaches?
[04:51] Jordan Kim: Standard is notification within 72 hours for confirmed data breaches affecting customer data; we can tighten that window in the DPA if needed.
[04:59] Emily Zhang: We'd like 48 hours if possible.
[05:02] Maya Patel: We'll take that back as a redline request.
[05:05] Sara Lopez: Can you also include contact points for escalation and an onboarding timeline? We have a December 2026 product launch target so procurement needs to lock vendor by mid-January.
[05:15] Maya Patel: Noted. Onboarding: typical Private/Dedicated onboarding takes 4-6 weeks from contract signature depending on infra; Hosted is faster - 1-2 weeks for initial keys and routes. We'll attach an onboarding checklist.
[05:27] Dr. Kevin Morrell: For testing we want a POC of 2 weeks with a bench of synthetic clinical prompts - can Redwood provide that under the trial terms?
[05:36] Jordan Kim: Yes, we can run a POC (proof of concept). We'll provision a sandbox environment with limited dataset and test harness; if you want model fine-tuning or evals we can include that in the SOW but that may affect timeline.
[05:50] Emily Zhang: Regarding liability caps - our legal is trying to negotiate higher caps for regulated workloads. What's Redwood's standard limitation of liability?
[05:58] Maya Patel: Standard is mutual caps tied to fees in the prior 12 months; for regulated workloads we can discuss adjustments - this is typically a commercial negotiation. We'll flag finance and legal to discuss.
[06:09] Sara Lopez: Payment terms - net 45 or net 30? We prefer net 60 in some cases - any flexibility?
[06:16] Maya Patel: We typically do net 30; for enterprise deals we can review net45/60 if needed - depends on procurement.
[06:22] Aaron Patel: One more technical question - cache/privacy: how long do you keep KV cache or prefixes? We need to ensure ephemeral caching isn't persistent storage of PHI.
[06:32] Jordan Kim: KV cache is in-memory and short-lived per session on our Hosted runtime; for Dedicated there are policies to flush KV cache and logs. We'll document cache retention and provide configuration options.
[06:44] Emily Zhang: Great. A few outstanding asks - redlined MSA/DPA with BYOK/KMS clause, SOC2 and pen test evidence, pricing sheet with committed tiers and term lock, and SLA table with p95 latency numbers.
[06:57] Maya Patel: Correct. We'll send all that. Any other blockers for procurement sign-off?
[07:02] Sara Lopez: Once we have redlines and pricing, finance needs two weeks to approve. Ideal contract signing by mid-January as mentioned.
[07:09] Maya Patel: Understood. We'll target sending materials by 2025-12-11.
[07:13] Dr. Kevin Morrell: Quick note on models - we want clarity on model versions and rollback policies if a model update causes regressions.
[07:20] Jordan Kim: We support model pinning and can do canary rollouts with automatic fallback to prior versions; we'll include rollout and model governance in the SOW.
[07:29] Emily Zhang: Okay that's helpful.
[07:31] Maya Patel: Wrap up - action items: we'll send redlines, SOC2 and pen test exec summary, pricing and SLA table, onboarding checklist, and schedule the legal follow-up for 2025-12-15. Any other follow-ups?
[07:44] Aaron Patel: Please include contact for security escalation.
[07:46] Liam Reyes: I'll add our security contact and escalation path in the onboarding doc.
[07:50] Sara Lopez: Thanks all, looking forward to the redline.
[07:53] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up by email shortly.
[07:56] [meeting end]
